branches.growth_obstruction: All marked 20x120 matrices have rank >=19 on P3. No nonzero pure tensor in a cubic overlap; thm:no-consecutive-pure-relations.
branches.single_opposite_symmetric: For singly opposite-symmetric standard AS windows all four evaluation ranks are at least three. A separated three-letter block gives exponential growth for a small odd evaluation. Both maximal-minor schemes coincide on the common even projective space, all four point correspondences are graphs, and four-shift is the identity without a finiteness assumption. The other half is canonically computed by the four-dimensional positive prolongation of the first window.

known_charts.regularity: A rank-ten, minimally two-periodic standard AS window with a reduced twenty-point scheme realizes two distinct simultaneous Veronese embeddings and is genuinely singly symmetric. Four normal quadratic parameters, a polynomial-module basis lift, quadratic nullhomotopies and depth prove all-degree exactness from a conditional degree-six test.
known_charts.current_result: Complete classification of the three-axis companion family. Regularity is equivalent to Delta=sum(a_i^2 a_j^2) nonzero; the rank-ten torus gives a two-dimensional image and exactly two active axes give bisymmetric rank eight. Every unmarked indexed isomorphism class is specified by the unordered projective triple of coefficient squares, including the positive-dimensional point-scheme boundary.

For Klein-graded singly symmetric windows with regular character spaces, having a simple fixed point forces the bisymmetric or the three-axis chart. If a character of H is absent, every regular window belongs to those charts or a two-plane-pair PBW chart, with an effective decision on all inputs. A rank-ten PBW example has skew point lines, outside the entire three-axis chart. Profile (3,1,1,1) forces full symmetry in AS.

The complete (2,2,1,1) Klein class of standard AS windows is covered by the bisymmetric chart and the closure of the single four-dimensional second-completion family. Singular cross blocks force bisymmetry for every AS tensor, including every thin zero pattern, and are effectively decided. All unequal completions with invertible cross blocks, even exceptional fibers or vanishing thin coefficients, lie in the same irreducible closure.
known_charts.rational_regular_input: The explicit rational matrices used for the twenty-point configuration are standard AS of minimal period four, with four central quartic parameters. See thm:klein-rational-period-four.
known_charts.generic_isomorphism: Four rational coefficients modulo at most sixteen character reindexings; the three projective point configurations have automorphism group Klein four and are mutually inequivalent. See sections/klein_generic_isomorphisms.tex.
known_charts.center_lift: On the rational two-dimensional slice v=4,w=6, the generic periodic quartic center has five generators as a vector space (character dimensions 3,2,0,0). A single Zariski-open neighborhood of the certified rational chart point b=2,c=3 consists entirely of standard regular closed fibers finite free of rank 256 per start over four central quartics. A finite constructible rank test recognizes this certificate on the whole second-completion closure.
known_charts.generic_center_and_PI: Over four algebraically independent second-completion parameters, the periodic quartic center has dimensions (3,2,0,0). One dense open containing the original rational point consists entirely of AS closed fibers finite free over four central quartics. Every standard AS point anywhere in this closure satisfies the uniform standard identity s_512.

known_charts.current_result: The full nondegenerate Klein (2,2,1,1) rank chart, including all coefficient-zero determinant fibers, is covered by the elliptic closure and the four exceptional presentations. If both determinant quadratics vanish identically the normalized base has eight explicit types, each with one bilinear equation for the entire fiber; all lie in the elliptic closure.
known_charts.unmarked_character_frames: The thin pencil and the branch divisor of the recovered quartic select a unique unmarked character frame at both full-rank samples and on their neighborhoods. Standard windows on this open are index-preservingly isomorphic exactly when one of 32 monomial permutations passes an integral torus test, including coefficient zeroes.
known_charts.quintic_defect: On both signed fixed elliptic curves at every ordinary characteristic-zero slope, the geometric support of the length-five defect equals that of the length-four defect. It consists of the twelve old sections and the four positive opposite-determinant sections, with the four negative pairs coincident when lambda squared times z equals minus one.

known_charts.current_result: With no Klein grading imposed, the singly symmetric rank-ten locus is smooth at the rational regular sample and has a fourteen-dimensional unmarked family, geometrically generically AS, with trivial projective indexed stabilizer and minimal period four. At this and the rank-sixteen sample the unrestricted normal tangents have dimensions (5,2,4,4) by character and all primary obstructions vanish. The extra alternating direction maps the opposite kernel isomorphically to its cokernel.

The zero-pairing boundary contains an entire non-AS bilinear curve at (z,lambda)=(3,2), with generic degree-six path dimensions (92,84,85,84), and a non-AS two-parameter sublocus x=z-1 with degree-four dimensions (35,36,36,35).

configuration_projection.result: The generic recovery degree from one projected configuration is exactly two. The two finite-edge AS windows are the original orientation and its reversal; one ordered first edge determines the extension. At both rational samples the same classification holds. A pencil of quartics with twenty triple points recovers every normalized square root, including the exclusion of degenerate Grassmann candidates.

finite_point_correspondences.scope: All four adjacent point schemes finite; no prescribed opposite rank.
finite_point_correspondences.reversible_component: At the reduced twenty-point control every square root is a sign translate. On the open of two rigid projections any all-four-finite AS extension has period dividing two, a four-dimensional cubic overlap and a unique invertible double-alternation kernel generator. A generic first relation space has no such extension. At the twenty-point example the exceptional locus has a unique local component of dimension 44, with orbit quotient dimension 14 and geometric generic regularity at opposite rank exactly eight and minimal period two. The symmetric stratum is the smooth 39-dimensional singular locus near this point, transverse to a rank-six quadratic cone.
finite_point_correspondences.open: Outside the dense smooth elliptic chart, residual components and general AS criteria remain open. The elliptic construction also includes special infinite point correspondences.

elliptic_reversible_chart.coverage: Dense open of reversible component, including additional special AS fibers, without imposing finite point correspondences.
elliptic_reversible_chart.regularity: All smooth genus-one data, integral nodal/cuspidal data and cyclic rational polygons with equal positive multidegrees, provided the pencil has no base point.
elliptic_reversible_chart.isomorphism: For L != M the two embedded apolar curves, their unique graph and the pencil recover ordered data.
elliptic_reversible_chart.residual: The algebraic criteria settle AS regularity and indexed isomorphism on this class. Complete moduli geometry and a uniform nonreduced graph interpretation are not asserted; nonsymmetric classes remain.
elliptic_reversible_chart.reduced_additive_boundary: All positive-degree multiple-point cases are AS exactly for equal multidegrees; ordered recognition for distinct bundles, m=2,3,4 quotient dimensions 13-m.
elliptic_reversible_chart.ribbon: Smooth conic ribbon: all fibers AS and complete ordered recognition for distinct bundles, quotient dimension nine.
elliptic_reversible_chart.reverse_recognition: Complete for bisymmetric adjacent-six/opposite-eight smooth-apolar tensors: standard AS iff the first relation six-plane avoids the Segre, and all such AS tensors have a unique elliptic pencil presentation up to ordered curve isomorphism.
elliptic_reversible_chart.nonreduced_boundary: All positive-degree pencils on nonreduced quartic complete intersections are AS; unequal bundles give ordered scheme-theoretic reconstruction. See sections/nonreduced_quartic_pencils.tex.
elliptic_reversible_chart.higher_rank: All bisymmetric adjacent-six AS tensors lie in the elliptic closure. Ranks nine and ten are excluded without further assumptions. A single smooth rank-eight apolar quartic suffices for a complete pure-relation and evaluation-rank criterion and forces the other apolar to be isomorphic.
elliptic_reversible_chart.integral_limit: All AS specializations retaining an integral quartic are invertible-pencil inputs on it. Noninvertible conductor pencils have a common quotient of exponential growth. See sections/binary_product_obstruction.tex.
elliptic_reversible_chart.polygon_limits: With two reduced limiting quadrics pencils and one nodal polygon, AS requires a common polygon with matching multidegrees. An additive opposite is excluded, including when the mixed multiplication loses one dimension.
elliptic_reversible_chart.all_reduced_limits: Two reduced quartic pencils force the same reduced curve and balanced ordered data for every AS specialization, including additive-additive projections; rank seven is excluded. At rank eight graph support for matched positive multidegrees with no pure relation is necessary and sufficient.
elliptic_reversible_chart.square_apolar: For a square in either opposite apolar kernel, the two axis evaluations must have rank three. The bisymmetric window is standard AS exactly for a ternary basepoint-free quadratic complete intersection. A two-periodic Ore presentation and the CI socle alternating form give opposite ranks six or eight only. In rank eight both kernel pencils coincide in aligned axes and explicit marked coefficient changes decide ordered isomorphism.
elliptic_reversible_chart.rank_dichotomy: All standard bisymmetric AS windows have opposite rank six or eight. Rank six is fully symmetrizable, and both rank-eight apolar pencils are quartic complete intersections. Factor partners are unique and opposite changes of coordinates are projectively equal in every rank. The transverse marked block has residual rank zero or two by PGL2 conjugation, while a radical line gives two coupled cubic forms and an alternating binary residual.
elliptic_reversible_chart.effective_recognition: Effective AS and ordered indexed isomorphism classification for all adjacent-rank-six bisymmetric reversing windows. A transverse distinct factor pair is regular exactly for nonassociative ternary multiplication, while a one-dimensional radical requires precisely its nonsingular binary relation. Ternary Clifford amalgams over the cubic binary algebra or the weighted polynomial algebra give all-degree Koszul and Frobenius proofs. Together with square and reduced-apolar recognition this covers every input in the class.
